ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, from left to right, there are three two-layer dartboards. In the first dartboard, all 3 darts land in the outer-ring region, and below it is labeled 12 Points. In the second dartboard, 2 darts land in the outer ring and 1 dart lands in the inner ring, and below it is labeled 15 Points. In the third dartboard, all 3 darts land in the inner ring, and below it is a question mark. Reasoning: Let the score for one hit in the outer ring be x, and the score for one hit in the inner ring be y. The first dartboard gives 3x = 12, so x = 4. The second dartboard gives 2x + y = 15. Substituting x = 4 gives 8 + y = 15, so y = 7. The third dartboard has all 3 darts in the inner ring, so the score is 3y = 3 × 7 = 21.

method.method_draft: Read the three target diagrams from left to right. In the first diagram, all 3 darts land in the outer field and the total shown is 12, so one outer-field hit is worth 12/3 = 4 points. In the second diagram, 2 darts land in the outer field and 1 dart lands in the inner field, and the total is 15, so the inner field is worth 15 - 2·4 = 7 points. In the third diagram, all 3 darts land in the inner field, so the score is 3·7 = 21.
